summary: I found no contradictions that stop the flow, only warnings. There is no `config/rtl_rules.md`, so the stack is just the default rules and nothing is overridden. I applied the style_lint change request by adding a `u_` alternative with the same 30-character limit to the signal-name-style regex. Section 2 requires `u_<function>` instance names, and Verible's signal-name-style also checks instance names. `verible_check_flags` accepted all the flags together, and `verible_lint` with the new signal-name-style regex gave no findings. The formatter only gets `--indentation_spaces=2` (FIL-03); the rules give no other layout values. The 30-character limit is enforced by the regexes, using `([x]?){N}` instead of `{m,n}` because a comma would break the flag. Many rules are about design meaning or constructs Verible has no rule for, so they are listed as not checkable.

findings.problem: ENM-03 lets an FSM skip the safe recovery state when the spec says the unused encodings are unreachable and the project accepts don't-care 'per COM-04'. COM-04 allows an 'x default only for a full-case `casez`. A plain `case` default must always assign a defined value. An FSM written with plain `case` (COM-03 default) can therefore never use the ENM-03 exception, and the exception only works if the state decode is a `casez`.
findings.suggestion: In ENM-03, change the exception to: "unless the spec states they are unreachable, the project accepts don't-care, and the state decode is a full-case `casez` per COM-04". Or drop the exception so every FSM always recovers.

findings.problem: COM-03 says every `case`/`casez` MUST have an explicit `default`, and also allows `unique case`. Verible's case-missing-default exempts `unique`/`unique0` case statements, so a `unique case` without a default passes lint. Only the generator and the judge can catch it.
findings.suggestion: Add to COM-03: "A `unique case` also has an explicit `default`." The judge then checks it, since Verible cannot.

findings.problem: P6 bans every plain `always`. Verible's always-comb only flags `always @*`, so `always @(posedge clk)` is not caught. The flags cover only part of P6.
findings.suggestion: No change to the rules. Q3TUI's code checks and the judge must cover the other plain `always` forms.

findings.problem: CMT-05 limits comment lines to 100 characters, but code lines have no limit. Verible's line-length cannot be limited to comments, so the flag (length 100) also applies to code lines, which is stricter than the rule.
findings.suggestion: Either accept 100 characters for all lines, or reword CMT-05 as "Any source line MUST NOT exceed 100 characters" so the rule matches what lint enforces.

findings.problem: NAM-07 (30 characters) is only half enforced. Verible checks ports, signals, parameters, localparams, enum type names, generate labels and instances (u_). It has no rule for module names, enum members (ENUM_*) or process labels (p_ff_/p_com_). Those lengths, and the module m_ pattern, are left to Q3TUI's code (max_len 30) and the judge.
findings.suggestion: No change to the rules. These names are checked by Q3TUI's naming profile (max_len 30, module_re, enum_re, proc_*_re), not by Verible.

findings.problem: Two examples do not follow the rules. NAM-05 uses `o_irq_n`, but `irq` is not in the NAM-08 table (NAM-04 allows only abbreviations from it, and the table gives `int` for interrupt). The TYP-02 inout example uses `PAD_W`, which does not follow the PARA_ pattern from the naming table.
findings.suggestion: In NAM-05 use an example that follows NAM-08 (for example `o_int_timer_n`), or add `irq` to the NAM-08 table. In the TYP-02 example write `io_pad` with `[PARA_PAD_W-1:0]`.

mapping: CMT-05: line-length=length:100 (Verible cannot limit comments only, so code lines are bounded too)
P6: always-comb (catches only `always @*`, not other plain `always` forms)
COM-03: case-missing-default (a `unique case` is exempt in Verible, though COM-03 asks for an explicit default)
P13: module-port, module-parameter (positional connections; `.*` is not checked)
P14: invalid-system-task-function (bans $random, $psprintf and similar; it is not an allow-list for the PAR-04 functions)
NAM-07 + Section 2 table (parameter names): parameter-name-style PARA_ (30 characters) and LPARA_ (30 characters)

NAM-07 + Section 2 table (signal names): signal-name-style i_/o_/io_/reg_/w_/u_ (30 characters) plus the loop index idx and genvar gen_idx; the u_ alternative was added from the style_lint change request and was proven with verible_lint (no findings)
